newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close higher, led by strong Telecom.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close higher, led by strong Telecom.

text.p: * NZ shares close firmer, Telecom provides impetus
* Restaurant Brands keenly traded
* Lion Nathan rollercoaster continues
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +5.75 at 2,362.78
352 nil * NZSC cap index +9.44 at 5,068.20
339 -3 * NZMC .NZMC midcap +2.79 at 1,871.72
362 -8 * Vol NZ$78 million, June futures +4 at 1187
708 +7 * Other movers - +10
Snedden said the latest phase of an ongoing $1 billion buyback was not the only reason for Telecom's strength and there was genuine interest in the stock.
"Other features were a large crossing of 1.3 million Fletcher Energy just before the close which was easily the largest deal of the day," Snedden said.
Fletcher Energy ended the day five cents stronger at $4.43 as the issue bounced off the selling triggered by news the Perdana Deep well in Brunei had found no significant hydrocarbons yet.

Brierley Investments firmed two cents on the back of a rise in its U.K. investment Thistle Hotels overnight and a good result from Australian-based James Hardie, while Lion Nathan continued its rollercoaster ride, now off eight cents after rising by a similar amount yesterday.

"There had been a major buyer in the market until their ex-dividend date on Monday, but when that buyer left it did seem to fall away, so yesterday may have been a dead cat bounce, as they say," Snedden said.
Restaurant Brands was keenly traded on its second day on the bourse, finishing level at $2.48 on turnover of 4.6 million shares, still well up on ots $2.20 issue price.
"It is a very, very healthy aftermarket," Snedden said.
Infratil rights at 4.7 cents, up one cent on turnover of 4.9 million, were also strongly traded. Infratil shares closed three cents better at $1.16.
